items.title: FPL GW11 BEST PLAYERS TO BUY! 🔴🇵🇹 CONSIDERING BRUNO F? #fpl  #premierleague
items.headline: Van Hecke leads Gameweek 11 defensive buys as Jackson tops the forward shortlist
items.summary:
Van Hecke is the leading defender target for Gameweek 11 because of his immediate fixtures, Double Gameweek appeal and attacking potential. Spurs are viewed as particularly strong defensively for their double, making Van Hecke the preferred short-term purchase. Vuskovic is another attractive option and is rated safer than Kai Penal, with a heavy upcoming schedule and the prospective returns of Minter and Matoma strengthening the case. Bournemouth's Antonio Silva completes the defensive shortlist thanks to strong long-term fixtures and Double Gameweek potential.

Midfield transfers are less straightforward, but Manzambi is a viable route into Aston Villa's attack for managers who already own Jackson and want to double up. Tavernier is a cheaper Bournemouth attacking option, especially for those unable to afford Evan Nelson, with Bournemouth's fixture run remaining favourable. However, Tavernier is on four yellow cards and carries a suspension risk. Pascal Gross is the standout midfield recommendation for non-owners: he is also one booking from a ban, but his form for Brighton and reliable minutes make him difficult to ignore.

Up front, Jackson is the preferred Gameweek 11 buy, with Sunderland at home and Aston Villa's upcoming fixtures driving the recommendation. Evan Nelson is next after scoring five goals in five matches, while Barry offers a budget alternative with appealing longer-term fixtures despite managers having missed his Gameweek 10 haul against Coventry. For a cheap goalkeeper, Spurs are the preferred source; Kinski is recommended for managers who cannot afford David Wright, given Spurs' defensive outlook and favourable short-term schedule.
key_points: Buy Van Hecke for the best short-term defensive fixture run, Double Gameweek potential and attacking threat.
Vuskovic is preferred to Kai Penal as a safer defensive pick with a busy schedule ahead and Minter and Matoma nearing returns.
Antonio Silva is a Bournemouth defensive option for managers targeting strong long-term fixtures and Double Gameweek upside.
Jackson is the top forward target for Gameweek 11, with Sunderland at home and Aston Villa's fixture run supporting the move.
Evan Nelson has scored five in five and remains a strong Bournemouth forward option, while Barry provides a cheaper long-term route.
Pascal Gross is a priority midfield buy for non-owners because of his Brighton form and secure minutes, but he is on four yellow cards.
Tavernier is also on four yellow cards, so his suspension risk must be considered before buying.
Kinski is the suggested budget goalkeeper if David Wright is unaffordable, with Spurs expected to offer short-term defensive value.

items.title: My transfer tips ahead of Gameweek 11 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Hold Mbeumo and Fernandes as Manchester United’s fixture run improves
items.summary:
Manchester United’s attack has underwhelmed, but selling Bryan Mbeumo or Bruno Fernandes ahead of Gameweek 11 is not advised. An expected improvement under Pochettino, combined with a favourable run from Gameweeks 12 to 15, gives owners reason to stay patient rather than use a transfer on an immediate exit.

Mohamed Salah has disappointed recently, but Everton at home is still a reasonable Gameweek 11 fixture and merits one more week of patience. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is more expendable because of the number of attractive forwards available: moving him to a player such as Ekitike or Nicolas Jackson is understandable. However, managers who can cover him may prefer to bench Calvert-Lewin this week and retain him for Coventry at home in Gameweek 12 and Ipswich at home in Gameweek 14.

Arsenal’s defensive situation remains uncertain. Kiwior is expected to start in Gameweeks 11 and 12, but he is not a recommended new purchase with William Saliba likely to return soon. Beyond David Raya, Gabriel is viewed as Arsenal’s only defender with genuinely dependable minutes, although he is a useful rather than essential option. Buying either Timber or Pascal Gross is acceptable this week, but both are one booking from a suspension.

Cole Palmer has not delivered value commensurate with his price, yet Leeds at home in Gameweek 11 and Crystal Palace at home in Gameweek 13 are enough to justify holding. Among Aston Villa midfielders, Morgan Rogers is preferred if fit; John McGinn is the cheaper alternative at £5.4m and offers penalty potential. Vuskovic is the safer long-term defensive pick because of his expected security of starts, while Kyper carries more upside but greater risk of losing his place. Cherki is also worth keeping for one more week, with Fulham at home a decent fixture and a likely start.
key_points: Keep Bryan Mbeumo and Bruno Fernandes despite Manchester United’s poor form, with Gameweeks 12-15 offering a favourable fixture run.
Hold Mohamed Salah for Everton at home in Gameweek 11 rather than selling after recent disappointing returns.
Selling Dominic Calvert-Lewin for Ekitike or Nicolas Jackson is viable, but benching him and targeting Coventry in Gameweek 12 and Ipswich in Gameweek 14 is also a valid route.
Avoid buying Kiwior despite probable starts in Gameweeks 11 and 12, as Saliba’s return threatens his minutes.
Gabriel is Arsenal’s most reliable outfield defensive option, while Raya remains the secure goalkeeper choice.
Timber and Pascal Gross are acceptable transfers but both sit one yellow card away from suspension.
Hold Cole Palmer through home fixtures against Leeds in Gameweek 11 and Crystal Palace in Gameweek 13.
Prefer Morgan Rogers among Aston Villa midfielders if fit; John McGinn is a £5.4m budget alternative with possible penalties.

items.title: MCGINN, FERNANDES + GABRIEL | THE FPL WATCHLIST GW11 WITH FPL HARRY 🔎 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Hold Palmer and Arsenal defenders as Bruno Fernandes decision waits on Manchester United’s new shape
items.summary:
The return from the international break begins a compressed FPL period of 10 gameweeks in 45 days, making patience valuable ahead of fresh team news and Manchester United’s first matches under their new manager. The recommended captain for the current round is Erling Haaland at home to Fulham, despite Manchester City’s uneven form and Haaland having only two double-digit returns so far. Nicolas Jackson is viewed as the standout forward buy for anyone needing an immediate replacement, while a Jackson captaincy is a stronger discussion for next week rather than now.

Arsenal’s defence is the major short-term dilemma. William Saliba has completed 90 minutes in a behind-closed-doors match after further Under-21 action, raising the prospect of Ezri Konsa losing starts soon. However, Konsa owners are advised not to sell pre-emptively: start him against Newcastle and react only if Saliba returns to the first team, as Konsa is unlikely to make damaging substitute appearances if omitted. Riccardo Calafiori is also a rotation concern after two 90-minute Italy outings and Arsenal’s run of Newcastle, Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Spurs, Real Madrid and Bournemouth. Gabriel remains the secure Arsenal defensive purchase, but managers should not force a move this week if it compromises more pressing plans.

The preferred approach is to retain Cole Palmer and roll transfers where possible, because next week may clarify both Arsenal’s selection and the best Manchester United attacker. Bruno Fernandes is the premium target if United’s new setup restores his output, with fixtures improving from Brentford, Newcastle, Coventry and Crystal Palace. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha are viable cheaper routes, but their roles and minutes need checking against Liverpool and in midweek first. Selling Palmer to Bruno may become the cleanest move; selling Palmer to Mbeumo or Cunha could instead release funds for Gabriel. United’s likely attacking improvement is acknowledged, but their defensive fragility and the risk of European rotation mean managers should wait for evidence rather than rush in.

Among value options, Pascal Gross remains a strong buy at £6.3m thanks to favourable fixtures and his bonus-point potential, while Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier is less appealing with four yellow cards. Aston Villa’s run against Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton, Crystal Palace and Coventry makes Morgan Rogers, Amadou Onana/Manzambi if fit, and John McGinn attractive differential routes; McGinn offers safer minutes, while Manzambi has greater haul potential but some fitness and rotation risk. At the back, Brighton’s Jan Paul van Hecke, Diego Coppola/Mahmoudovic, Luka Vuskovic and Silva are preferred dependable alternatives to uncertain Arsenal minutes, with Van Hecke particularly attractive for his attacking threat and Ipswich fixture. Joao Pedro’s fitness is important: if unavailable, selling him for Dominic Calvert-Lewin ahead of Coventry at home can help fund a Palmer-to-Bruno move.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham at home; Jackson is the only serious alternative captaincy conversation, but more likely for next gameweek.
Do not sell Ezri Konsa solely because Saliba has played 90 minutes behind closed doors; play him against Newcastle and reassess after Arsenal’s Dortmund match.
Gabriel is the safest Arsenal defender for minutes, while Calafiori is a plausible rotation risk during Arsenal’s demanding Premier League and Champions League schedule.
Roll a transfer and keep Cole Palmer where possible, with Palmer-to-Bruno Fernandes potentially the key move after Manchester United show their new tactical setup.
Mbeumo and Cunha are watchlist alternatives to Bruno, but their roles under the new Manchester United manager need confirming before investment.
Pascal Gross remains the preferred mid-price midfielder; avoid rushing into Tavernier while he sits on four yellow cards.
Aston Villa midfielders are strong fixture-based differentials, with McGinn safer for minutes and Manzambi offering more explosive potential if passed fit.
If Joao Pedro is ruled out, Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a useful short-term replacement for Coventry at home and can unlock funds for Bruno Fernandes.

items.title: Is selling Haaland soon crazy? 🤔 FPL Gameweek 11 Preview 🔥
items.headline: Haaland remains the Gameweek 11 captain despite tempting Ekitike differential
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear captaincy call for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham. He has blanked in his last two, but nine goals in 10 matches and Manchester City's attacking strength make him difficult to oppose in a favourable home fixture. Ekitike is the leading alternative against a Manchester United defence conceding 1.79 xG per game, although uncertainty over penalties makes him less secure than Haaland. Jackson is a weaker option without spot-kicks, while Palmer's form and underlying numbers do not justify captaining him against Leeds. De Kuyper is the ultra-differential captain, with Brighton carrying clean-sheet and attacking-return potential against Hull, but Haaland remains the recommendation.

A Free Hit in Gameweek 11 is generally discouraged because most squads should already be well set up. It should not be used simply to gain information on Joao Pedro's fitness or potential yellow-card suspensions for players such as Tair, Gross and Silva; managers should wait for those events before committing the chip. A strong Free Hit draft includes Kinsky; Van Hecke, Vuskovic and De Kuyper alongside a Spurs defensive double-up; Gross, Palmer, Rogers and Kudus; plus Ekitike, Haaland and Jackson. Even so, the chip is likely more valuable in a later, more problematic week.

For a Gameweek 11 Wildcard, the preferred build prioritises Haaland and Bruno Fernandes, even at the cost of Arsenal defensive coverage. Kinsky and Trafford offer a cheaper rotating goalkeeper pair than Raya, while Van Hecke, Silva, Vuskovic, De Kuyper and Murmurovic provide a strong group of roughly £5m defenders. Silva is one booking from suspension, but the squad depth should absorb it. Calafiori and Konsa carry rotation risks, and Gabriel is difficult to afford alongside Haaland and Fernandes. Managers who prefer Arsenal security can instead select Raya and Gabriel by downgrading Fernandes, potentially to Gibbs-White.

Wildcard timing is team-dependent, though Gameweeks 16-17 offer a notable fixture upswing for Arsenal and Liverpool. Arsenal's run from Gameweek 16 includes Manchester United, Crystal Palace, Fulham, Ipswich and Brentford, while Liverpool have a long favourable stretch and are viable purchases even sooner. Fernandes is attractive from Gameweek 12 given Manchester United's fixtures, while Mbeumo, Gibbs-White and Florian Wirtz are midfield alternatives. Joao Pedro is worth monitoring as a high-upside differential if fit, but spending two or three transfers to buy him immediately is too aggressive after two injuries and ahead of Forest away in Gameweek 12.

Selling Haaland for Gameweek 12, when City visit Arsenal, is a viable differential strategy rather than an automatic mistake, especially if it funds Fernandes and another premium forward. However, Haaland is still likely the preferred captain in Gameweeks 13, 15 and 16, and possibly four of the next six rounds overall. His reliable minutes, penalties and ceiling make him hard to remove; the safer approach is to retain him and find another route to Fernandes where possible. Managers should preserve transfers ahead of the festive period, when injuries, rotation and yellow-card suspensions become more disruptive, but do not need three strong bench players every week.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham in Gameweek 11; Ekitike is the best alternative but lacks confirmed penalty duty.
Avoid using the Free Hit merely to wait for Joao Pedro news or yellow cards; most teams do not need the chip in Gameweek 11.
A Gameweek 11 Wildcard can favour Haaland and Bruno Fernandes over Arsenal defenders, using Kinsky and Trafford as a budget goalkeeper rotation.
Raya and Gabriel remain the preferred Arsenal defensive combination for managers willing to sacrifice Fernandes or other spending.
Target Arsenal and Liverpool more heavily from Gameweeks 16-17, although Liverpool assets are already viable buys before then.
Do not spend two or three transfers rushing Joao Pedro back; monitor his minutes and fitness after two injuries.
Gibbs-White is a strong Christmas-period target because of penalties, secure minutes and a favourable fixture run after Bournemouth away.
Hold Haaland unless fully committed to a differential Gameweek 12 plan, as he remains a leading captain for Gameweeks 13, 15 and 16.

items.title: BEST DEFCON PLAYERS 💪 | FPL DEFCON DEEP DIVE WITH TOM HADLEY 📝 | GAMEWEEK 11 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bournemouth centre-backs Silva and Hill emerge as DefCon double-up targets
items.summary:
Bournemouth defenders Anthony Silva and James Hill stand out as the strongest DefCon options, combining frequent defensive contributions with a team that ranks among the league's best for recent defensive data. Silva costs £5.1m and Hill £5.6m, and both regularly contend for bonus as well as the two-point DefCon threshold. With Nottingham Forest, Fulham, Hull and Coventry among their next six opponents, a short-term double-up is viable for managers who want clean-sheet and DefCon upside, although Brighton and Arsenal temper the run.

Aston Villa have the best fixture run over the next five or six gameweeks, but their defenders are less reliable DefCon picks under Unai Emery. Victor Lindelof has recently posted strong numbers, while Pau Torres also reaches the threshold, yet Villa's tendency to control easier matches can reduce the clearances, blocks and other actions needed for DefCon. They are therefore more appealing for clean sheets than as dependable defensive-action assets. Arsenal remain a premium route: Gabriel offers regular starts, DefCon potential and a useful place to park funds, while Konsa has hit DefCon in four of his eight Arsenal starts despite uncertainty over his place when Saliba returns.

The broader defensive template remains formidable, with Maremavich, Van Hecke, Silva and Hill all offering regular DefCon returns at relatively accessible prices. However, £4.0m Hull defender Mendy is highlighted as a future enabler: he has reached DefCon whenever he has completed 90 minutes and could become essential if managers need funds for premium midfielders such as Bruno Fernandes. Crystal Palace's Chris Richards is a wait-and-see option ahead of a managerial change, while Nottingham Forest's Murillo has strong underlying defensive numbers, favourable Christmas fixtures and bonus-point pedigree. Liverpool's schedule through Gameweek 20 also brings Virgil van Dijk into consideration, potentially alongside Jota, with Sunderland, Leeds, Hull and Coventry featuring prominently.

In midfield, the DefCon names are largely bench-cover options rather than priority buys. Kobbie Mainoo has hit the threshold in every start, while Palacios, Moises Caicedo and Alexis Mac Allister provide cheap, steady routes to four-point returns. Tavernier is particularly encouraging because he consistently gets close to DefCon while retaining attacking threat. For Villa, John McGinn is preferred for returns and penalties, but £4.9m Allison is a viable differential despite uncertain minutes across Villa's midfield options.

Bruno Fernandes is the main potential disruptor to the current template. Manchester United's fixtures are poor overall until Gameweek 20, but the Gameweek 14 home match against Coventry offers a plausible captaincy punt, especially if a new manager sparks improvement. Fernandes remains difficult to fund without sacrificing players such as Gabriel or Rogers, so a Free Hit in Gameweek 14 may be a cleaner way to exploit the fixture. His elite historical ceiling, strong baseline bonus numbers and captaincy appeal mean one major haul could quickly trigger a widespread transfer rush.
key_points: Anthony Silva and James Hill are strong Bournemouth targets for Gameweeks 14 and 16, with Hull and Coventry at home offering a credible clean-sheet and DefCon double-up opportunity.
Villa's fixtures are excellent, but Lindelof and Pau Torres are less dependable for DefCon because Emery's side can dominate easier matches without generating enough defensive actions.
Gabriel is a premium Arsenal defender with regular DefCon potential, while Konsa posts an excellent four DefCon hits in eight Arsenal starts but faces a possible minutes threat from Saliba.
Hull's £4.0m Mendy is a leading budget enabler because he reaches DefCon whenever he plays 90 minutes and can finance future moves for Bruno Fernandes or other premiums.
Murillo is a watchlist differential for Forest's favourable Christmas run, combining reliable minutes, DefCon potential, bonus appeal and occasional goal threat.
Liverpool top the fixture ticker through Gameweek 20, making Van Dijk and a possible defensive double-up worth considering from Gameweek 15 or 17.
Bruno Fernandes is best viewed as a Gameweek 14 Coventry captaincy punt or Free Hit target rather than an immediate long-term buy, given Manchester United's difficult surrounding fixtures.
Tavernier, Mainoo, Palacios and Caicedo offer cheap midfield DefCon coverage, but McGinn and Allison carry more appeal where managers need attacking upside.

items.title: TOP 5K OVERALL RANK 🔥 | THE FPL SCOUTCAST GAMEWEEK 11 🚨 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Erling Haaland is the clear captain as FPL managers weigh defensive depth against festive rotation
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham, despite Manchester City’s recent drop in form. City have the highest projected goal total of the round and Haaland remains third for expected goal involvement over the past six weeks, behind Everton’s Thierno Barry and Bournemouth’s Evanilson. Cole Palmer at home to Leeds and Alexander Isak away to Liverpool are alternatives, but Leeds are viewed as a potentially stubborn opponent and Haaland’s price, home fixture and ceiling make him the sensible default. His appeal may diminish immediately afterwards with Arsenal away, creating scope to oppose him in later weeks.

The strongest squad-building theme remains investing in defence. Arsenal continue to lead clean-sheet projections by a distance, making David Raya, Gabriel, Piero Hincapie/Calafiori and Cristian Mosquera-style coverage highly valuable, although William Saliba’s eventual return creates uncertainty around Cristhian Concer’s place. Concer is still worth holding until he is actually displaced, rather than transferring pre-emptively. Managers without Raya or a secure route to triple Arsenal defence can instead lean on Bournemouth, Brighton and Liverpool defenders: Marcos Senesi-type DefCon options, Antonio Silva, Illia Zabarnyi/Vuskovic, Jan Paul van Hecke and Liverpool’s Joe Gomez offer regular minutes, favourable fixtures and defensive-contribution upside.

Brighton’s Vuskovic is backed as a strong long-term pick despite not matching the elite DefCon consistency of the very best centre-backs. He offers clean-sheet potential in a reliable Brighton side plus occasional attacking returns, while his underlying DefCon numbers remain respectable. Bournemouth’s fixtures also support Evanilson and Marcus Tavernier consideration, with Forest, Brighton, Hull and Coventry among the upcoming opponents. Evanilson’s recent returns include considerable goalkeeper-assisted fortune, but he looks secure for minutes and benefits from Bournemouth’s improving attack as Kroupi returns. Barry is the cheaper alternative at £5.7m: his finishing can look unconvincing, but Everton funnel chances through him and his price allows managers to field four or five premium defensive assets.

The seven Gameweeks from 11 to 17 arrive in little more than a month, with league midweeks and European commitments increasing rotation risk. Reliable minutes are therefore prized: Morgan Rogers, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Pascal Gross, Haaland, Barry and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are seen as dependable core picks, while Morgan Gibbs-White’s guaranteed minutes and penalties are offset by Nottingham Forest’s poor form. Villa’s Manzambi is a greater concern, having already carried uncertain minutes and facing a demanding first festive period in England. Tavernier and Evanilson also have some rotation risk because of Bournemouth’s European schedule. With squads broadly well set up, the preferred approach is to roll transfers where possible, retain flexibility and reassess Arsenal defensive slots once Saliba’s league involvement becomes clearer.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 11 against Fulham; Palmer and Isak are viable but less convincing alternatives.
Hold Concer until Saliba actually takes his starting place rather than selling him on speculation.
Arsenal remain the best clean-sheet bet through Gameweek 16, but Bournemouth, Brighton and Liverpool defenders provide strong alternatives for managers unable to reach triple Arsenal coverage.
Vuskovic is a recommended Brighton defender for their fixture run, combining solid minutes, clean-sheet potential and some attacking upside.
Barry is a useful £5.7m third striker because Everton create heavily through him, although his recent returns contain some luck and his fixtures become less appealing.
Evanilson has favourable Bournemouth fixtures and secure-looking starts, but managers should not overstate his recent scoring run after several goalkeeper errors.
Manzambi is a rotation risk during the congested Gameweeks 11-17, while Rogers, Gross, Dewsbury-Hall, Barry and Calvert-Lewin offer more dependable minutes.
Rolling transfers is favoured for well-set squads, preserving flexibility for festive rotation, yellow-card suspensions and possible fixture disruption.

items.title: FPL GW11 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 11 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: Haaland is the standout captain as Fulham visit and Jackson leads the transfer buys
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains an emphatic keep and the leading captaincy choice for the home meeting with Fulham, despite consecutive blanks. His underlying numbers remain strong and the fixture is too attractive to abandon a premium forward. Alexander Isak is also a keep against Manchester United, while Kieran Trippier remains worth holding through a useful Newcastle schedule. Cheap forwards Costas Las and Havertz can survive for their immediate fixtures, but neither is a priority long-term pick; João Pedro and Brobbey require late fitness checks before a decision is made.

The recommended forward sales are Gonzalo and Yoane Wissa, who have failed to produce a goal or assist in the past six gameweeks and now face difficult schedules. Wissa also carries possible rotation concerns, while Thiago is an immediate sell because of suspension. For new purchases, Haaland heads the list, with Jackson the preferred alternative or partner thanks to excellent Aston Villa fixtures against Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton and Crystal Palace. Evan Nelson offers good form and numbers but has tougher opponents and more minutes risk, while Isak is a viable higher-priced alternative. Barry is the cheap forward to monitor rather than buy immediately because Brentford and Liverpool come next.

Midfield is described as a thin market, making Tavernier and Morgan Rogers sensible holds rather than exciting options. Tavernier keeps finding high-quality chances despite low shot volume, while Rogers becomes particularly appealing for Crystal Palace at home in Gameweek 13. Bryan Mbeumo is worth retaining on underlying data and could simply be benched against Liverpool. Palmer is a monitor: his penalty duty and Crystal Palace fixture offer upside, but his non-penalty attacking numbers are far too weak for a £9.8m asset. Bruno Fernandes is similarly divisive under new management, while Cherki is only viable for managers comfortable with unpredictable rotation. Pascal Gross is the clearest midfield buy due to penalties, set pieces, secure minutes and fixtures against Hull and Newcastle; Florian Wirtz is a differential Liverpool option at £7.2m.

Defence offers the strongest transfer market. Brighton defenders Veltman and De Kuyper are leading buys for favourable clean-sheet fixtures, with Veltman preferred for set pieces, defensive-contribution potential and reliable centre-back minutes. Gabriel is the premium Arsenal defender to target long term, while Van Hecke is an excellent alternative for Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham if Brighton coverage is already in place or Gabriel is unaffordable. Existing Arsenal defenders can be held against Newcastle, but Konsa is not a new buy because Saliba's return is likely to displace him soon. Raya and Verbruggen are the only recommended goalkeeper purchases; Pickford is expendable because of price and fixtures, and Aston Villa goalkeeper Suzuki is avoided despite a kind schedule because Villa's defensive numbers are poor.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham at home; consecutive blanks do not outweigh his underlying numbers or fixture.
Buy Jackson ahead of Aston Villa's run against Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton and Crystal Palace, with Evan Nelson a cheaper but less secure alternative.
Sell Gonzalo, Wissa and suspended Thiago; Gonzalo and Wissa have no attacking returns across the past six gameweeks and face poor fixtures.
Keep Tavernier, Rogers and Mbeumo in a weak midfield market, although Mbeumo can be benched against Liverpool.
Monitor Palmer rather than automatically keeping or buying him: penalties help, but his open-play xG and xA do not justify £9.8m.
Prioritise Veltman or De Kuyper in defence, with Gabriel the preferred premium Arsenal purchase and Van Hecke a strong alternative.
Do not buy Konsa now, as Saliba's likely return threatens his Arsenal starting role; Ben White also has major rotation risk.
Buy Raya if budget allows or Verbruggen for value; avoid Suzuki and consider selling Pickford.

items.title: THE BEST FPL GW11 FREE HIT DRAFT TEMPLATE! 🍟 #fpl  #premierleague  #fantasypremierleague #football
items.headline: Haaland leads Gameweek 11 Free Hit as Isak and Kudus provide differential upside
items.summary:
A Gameweek 11 Free Hit draft is built around Erling Haaland as captain, while largely avoiding Arsenal’s outfield assets despite their appeal. David Raya is the only Arsenal player in the starting XI, with the selection instead chasing upside through attacking punts and favourable home fixtures.

The defence includes a Brighton double-up featuring Kuiper and Vuskovic, alongside Jan Paul van Hecke, who is backed to profit from Brighton’s home match against Ipswich. The aggressive structure carries obvious risk compared with a safer Arsenal defensive double-up. A more conservative 4-3-3 could bring in Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori or Ezri Konsa and lean more heavily on Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential.

Midfield is where the Free Hit takes its biggest swings. Pascal Gross is selected for the trip to Hull, Mohammed Kudus is favoured at home to Ipswich as Spurs’ leading attacking threat, and Churkey is included against Fulham despite not being a secure weekly starter. Man Zambia completes the midfield in a home fixture against Sunderland.

Haaland is joined up front by Jackson and Alexander Isak. Isak faces Manchester United at home and remains a calculated pick despite the possibility that United improve after the international break; his recent form and home fixture are considered enough to justify the selection. Haaland remains the preferred captain, but Jackson or Isak offer viable differential alternatives, while Churkey is the high-risk, high-reward rogue captain option.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the primary Gameweek 11 captain in the Free Hit draft.
David Raya is the only Arsenal starter, with the draft prioritising punts over an Arsenal defensive double-up.
Jan Paul van Hecke is backed for Brighton’s home fixture against Ipswich, alongside a Brighton defensive double-up of Kuiper and Vuskovic.
A safer alternative is a 4-3-3 with Gabriel or Riccardo Calafiori, plus Ezri Konsa, to increase defensive security.
Mohammed Kudus is a key midfield pick at home to Ipswich because he is viewed as Spurs’ main attacking threat.
Churkey is a differential against Fulham but carries minutes risk because he does not start every match.
Alexander Isak is retained for Manchester United at home, with his form and fixture outweighing concerns over a post-international-break United improvement.
Jackson, Isak and Churkey are differential captaincy options for managers willing to move away from Haaland.

items.title: WHO IS THE BEST ASTON VILLA MIDFIELDER? 🦁 🟣 FPL GW11 #fpl #premierleague #astonvilla
items.headline: John McGinn emerges as Aston Villa’s value alternative to Nicholas Jackson
items.summary:
Aston Villa’s fixture run makes their attack a priority target over the next five gameweeks, with Nicholas Jackson the clear first-choice signing for managers who do not already own him. The schedule is strong enough to justify investment, but the alternatives require more caution because each carries either fitness or minutes risk.

Manzambi is an attractive option if he is passed fit. He withdraws from the Switzerland international squad and remains yellow-flagged, but the expectation is that he is being rested after playing through an issue for around a month rather than facing a major absence. If available, he offers a strong route into Villa’s attack during the favourable run.

Allison is the least appealing of the main alternatives because of rotation concerns. Villa face significant Champions League ties against Galatasaray and PSG alongside their Premier League fixtures, creating a realistic chance that league minutes are managed. Those European commitments make his upside less reliable despite the domestic schedule.

John McGinn is the preferred budget alternative at £5.4m. He starts nine of Villa’s 10 matches this season, and even in the one match he does not start he arrives at half-time when the side struggles without him. McGinn also carries set-piece threat and can share penalties when Emiliano Buendía and Ross Barkley are absent. He is not without risk, but his price, security of starts and multiple routes to returns make him the best non-Jackson Villa option.
key_points: Nicholas Jackson is the priority Aston Villa attacker for the upcoming five-game fixture run.
Manzambi is a strong pick if fit, with his Switzerland withdrawal expected to be a recovery measure rather than a major injury concern.
Allison carries the biggest rotation risk because Champions League matches against Galatasaray and PSG could affect his Premier League minutes.
John McGinn is the preferred Villa alternative at £5.4m after starting nine of 10 matches this season.
McGinn offers set pieces and potential penalty involvement when Buendía and Ross Barkley do not play.
Villa’s favourable fixtures support attacking investment, but managers must balance that upside against European rotation and fitness uncertainty.

items.title: Keep or Sell Man United attackers 🤔 FPL GW11 Transfer Tips 🔥
items.headline: Hold Bruno Fernandes and Mbeumo as Pochettino’s Manchester United fixtures turn in Gameweek 12
items.summary:
Manchester United’s trip to Liverpool in Gameweek 11 is not the time to buy into a new-manager bounce, but existing owners of Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are advised to hold. United’s league position is poor, yet their underlying attack is already among the top five for expected goals and Pochettino should bring some improvement. More importantly, Brentford at home, Newcastle away, Coventry at home and Crystal Palace away follow from Gameweek 12. Fernandes remains the secure minutes option, while Mbeumo and Cunha are attractively priced but carry uncertainty over roles and whether they retain 90-minute starts. Their fixtures also offer alternative captaincy routes when Erling Haaland faces Arsenal in Gameweek 12 and Brentford in Gameweek 14.

Kevin Schade is not a forced sale despite a run without an attacking return since Gameweek 5. His minutes have risen steadily following a shoulder issue, reaching 90 minutes last time out, and Everton at home in Gameweek 11 is a reasonable fixture. Rolling a transfer and reassessing before tougher matches against Arsenal and Manchester City is preferred, although selling for an in-form alternative such as Tavanier, Manzambi or John McGinn is defensible. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is similarly a hold where squad depth permits: Chelsea, Manchester City and Liverpool away are difficult, but Coventry at home in Gameweek 12 and Ipswich at home in Gameweek 14 are strong fixtures. A direct upgrade to Ekitike or Nicolas Jackson is appealing, particularly given Jackson’s excellent five-game run, but otherwise benching Calvert-Lewin in the hardest games is preferable to selling. That logic changes if a Free Hit in Gameweek 12 or 14 is locked in, as it removes one of his useful home fixtures.

Arsenal’s defence remains excellent but is no longer essential, particularly because rotation clouds most picks. Gabriel is the only outfield defender considered reliably secure for league minutes and offers clean-sheet, goal and defensive-contribution potential; he is a long-term purchase for managers willing to commit funds to defence. Riccardo Calafiori should start against Newcastle in Gameweek 11 but is unlikely to play every match through a congested run including Manchester City, Spurs and Real Madrid, while the return of Saliba threatens Ezri Konsa’s place. Konsa owners can reasonably use him for Gameweeks 11 and 12, but non-owners should avoid buying at £4.9m and choose cheaper alternatives such as Van Hecke, Vuskovic, De Kyper or Murmović instead.

Villa’s fixtures from Gameweek 11 are highly favourable, making McGinn a viable £5.4m enabler. He has acceptable open-play numbers, may take penalties when Buendia and Barkley are absent, and faces Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton, Crystal Palace and Coventry. Manzambi is marginally preferred if fully fit at £6.2m, but his recurring calf concern and potential reduced minutes in the midweek Gameweek 13 schedule matter; McGinn is the simpler cheaper route. Among Brighton defenders, Vuskovic is the safer long-term pick for minutes, while De Kyper has the greater attacking appeal if he holds his place. Finally, Ryan Cherki is a hold for Fulham at home in Gameweek 11 after another goal, but not a buy and likely a Gameweek 12 sale ahead of Arsenal away and a congested period that heightens his minutes risk.
key_points: Hold Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo through Liverpool away if already owned, then reassess Manchester United’s attack after two Pochettino-era matches before Gameweek 12.
Do not buy Manchester United attackers in Gameweek 11, but keep Mbeumo and Cunha on the watchlist as affordable captaincy alternatives for Haaland’s tougher Gameweeks 12 and 14.
Kevin Schade is a reasonable hold for Everton at home because his minutes are improving, though he becomes a stronger sell or bench candidate from Gameweek 13.

Keep Dominic Calvert-Lewin where possible and cover his difficult away fixtures, but direct moves to Ekitike or Nicolas Jackson are credible upgrades; sell more readily if a Gameweek 12 or 14 Free Hit is certain.
Gabriel is Arsenal’s only dependable outfield defensive buy; avoid purchasing Calafiori or Konsa amid expected rotation and Saliba’s return.
John McGinn is a £5.4m Villa enabler with favourable fixtures and likely penalty responsibility, while Manzambi is slightly preferable only if declared fully fit.
Vuskovic is the safer Brighton defensive transfer for long-term minutes, whereas De Kyper is the higher-upside choice for managers with spare transfers.
Hold Ryan Cherki for Fulham at home in Gameweek 11 if waiting for line-ups is feasible, but plan to sell before Arsenal away in Gameweek 12.

items.title: BRING IN FERNANDES? 🤔 | FPL GENERAL'S GAMEWEEK 11 TEAM REVEAL ✅ | FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes becomes a Gameweek 14 target as Manchester United’s new-manager bounce is tested
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 plans remain conservative after the international break. The recommended move is to sell Joško Gvardiol for Brighton defender Vuskovic, creating a Brighton triple-up and allowing Dominic Calvert-Lewin to sit on the bench in a 4-4-2. Calvert-Lewin’s poor away record makes him expendable from the starting XI, while Vuskovic offers attacking potential, clean-sheet points and DefCon upside. Arsenal’s Raya, Calafiori and Konsa are retained for now, with Konsa treated as a £4.5m-style squad player who can be benched if his starts become insecure; Nico Williams is the likely next defensive sale.

Erling Haaland is the clear Gameweek 11 captain at home to Fulham, despite Manchester City’s uneven form. The advice is not to overthink a favourable home fixture immediately after an international break, although captaincy becomes much more open thereafter. Nicolas Jackson away to Ipswich in Gameweek 12, Alexander Isak at home to Sunderland in Gameweek 13, and Bournemouth assets against Hull in Gameweek 14 all enter the discussion. Haaland at home to Hull in Gameweek 16 stands out as another straightforward armband choice and a possible Triple Captain opportunity.

Manchester United’s appointment of Mauricio Pochettino puts Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha under scrutiny, but the fixture run argues against an immediate investment. Liverpool away, Brentford at home and Newcastle away provide a useful test of whether the team improves before Coventry visit in Gameweek 14. Bruno is attractive for that single fixture and captaincy opportunity, but his £11.6m price makes him difficult to buy without sacrificing premium defenders, forwards or value midfielders. Mbeumo is viewed as the best current United pick at £7.9m, while Cunha is an appealing alternative if he receives regular minutes. Managers with a Free Hit can target Bruno plus other United players in Gameweek 14; those without it can consider moving Cole Palmer to Bruno if United show genuine improvement.

Crystal Palace also warrant monitoring following their managerial change, with Thomas Frank strongly linked and a favourable immediate run beginning at Coventry and home to Hull. Jean-Philippe Mateta has strong underlying numbers but must first serve his suspension, making him a watchlist option rather than a short-term transfer. In defence, Chris Richards and Tosin Adarabioyo offer cheap DefCon routes, while Khalil is an attacking wing-back differential. Pino and Kamada have shown some output at modest prices, but Palace midfielders face stiff competition from established value picks such as Pascal Gross, Marcus Tavernier and Morgan Rogers. Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper is also increasingly worth captaincy consideration: he effectively plays as an attacker, leads the game for points and combines attacking returns with clean-sheet potential, though his tendency to be substituted around 60 minutes limits his ceiling.
key_points: Sell Joško Gvardiol for Brighton’s Vuskovic in Gameweek 11, bench Dominic Calvert-Lewin and play a 4-4-2.
Captain Erling Haaland against Fulham in Gameweek 11; Gameweek 16 at home to Hull is the standout future Haaland Triple Captain candidate.
Bruno Fernandes is not a Wildcard priority before Liverpool, Brentford and Newcastle, but Gameweek 14 at home to Coventry is a major target.
Bryan Mbeumo is the preferred Manchester United attacker on current value, with Matheus Cunha the next-best alternative if his minutes improve.
A Gameweek 14 Free Hit can exploit Manchester United’s Coventry fixture without committing to Bruno Fernandes long term.
Cole Palmer can be sold to fund Bruno Fernandes around Gameweek 14, particularly with Chelsea facing Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa in the surrounding weeks.
Monitor Crystal Palace under a potential Thomas Frank appointment; Mateta, Chris Richards, Tosin Adarabioyo and Khalil are the principal watchlist names.
Maxim De Cuyper deserves consideration as a Brighton captaincy differential because of his attacking role, clean-sheet potential and current points total.

items.title: TOP 10 FPL GW11 MIDFIELDERS TO BUY! 💰 PALMER OUT? 🥶 #fpl  #premierleague  #chelsea
items.headline: Pascal Groß tops the Gameweek 11 midfield shortlist as reliable minutes drive the picks
items.summary:
Pascal Groß is the leading midfield target for Gameweek 11 because of his near-guaranteed minutes and consistent role. Tavernier ranks second as another dependable long-term option who usually plays 90 minutes, although managers need to note that he sits on four yellow cards and is one booking from a suspension. Morgan Rogers completes the top three; despite managers moving away from Cole Palmer, Rogers is still viewed as a strong buy.

Aston Villa assets feature prominently. Manzambi is backed as a budget midfield option for managers who want to double up on Villa’s attack alongside Jackson, with an encouraging fixture run strengthening the case. Morgan Gibbs-White is also a viable mid-priced pick: his regular 90-minute appearances, set-piece involvement and penalty duties offset doubts over his value, while his upcoming fixtures improve.

Florian Wirtz is recommended as a longer-term Liverpool midfield investment despite debate over his FPL appeal. His performances are considered to have improved over the past couple of months, and Liverpool’s fixtures support patience. Bruno Fernandes is a more speculative option, with the prospect of a new-manager bounce at Manchester United potentially lifting his output, though his price remains the central concern. Bryan Mbeumo is preferred to Matheus Cunha because of his advanced role up front or on the wing, even though Cunha has produced more recent returns.

At the cheaper end, Juju Hall is an Everton alternative for managers unable to afford Barry, with Everton’s longer-term fixtures looking favourable. Rodoni narrowly gets the nod over Balumi for the final budget spot because he is on penalties and is considered the more reliable option, while Balumi carries a minor injury concern.
key_points: Pascal Groß is the preferred Gameweek 11 midfielder because he offers reliable 90-minute appearances.
Tavernier is a strong long-term pick but is on four yellow cards and one caution away from suspension.
Morgan Rogers remains a recommended buy even as some managers sell Palmer-related assets.
Manzambi offers a cheap route into Aston Villa’s promising fixture run, particularly alongside Jackson.
Morgan Gibbs-White benefits from penalties, set pieces and improving fixtures, although his price is a consideration.
Bruno Fernandes is a higher-risk option whose appeal depends on a possible Manchester United new-manager bounce.
Bryan Mbeumo is preferred to Matheus Cunha for his more advanced role, despite Cunha’s stronger recent returns.
Rodoni is favoured over Balumi among budget picks due to penalty duties and Balumi’s injury concern.

items.title: FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW11 ✅
items.headline: Haaland is the Gameweek 11 captain as Jackson and Brighton assets lead the buy list
items.summary:
Manchester City’s home match against Fulham makes Erling Haaland the clear Gameweek 11 captaincy favourite, while Nicolas Jackson is the standout forward alternative after a run of returns in five of his last six matches. Jackson’s schedule — Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton, Palace and Coventry — is among the best in the game, making a Haaland-Jackson front two the preferred structure. The third forward slot is best filled cheaply by Barry or Evanilson, with Barry marginally preferred for value after posting 7.76 expected goal involvements, second only to Haaland.

Brighton are heavily backed for their trip to Hull. Gross is an exceptional midfield option after producing 10 goal involvements in 10 matches, aided by penalties and set pieces, while defenders De Cuyper, Van Hecke and Vuskovic benefit from strong clean-sheet prospects and attacking threat. De Cuyper remains worth holding despite Mitoma’s potential return, as he may retain his place in Brighton’s successful current setup, but Vuskovic is the safer new purchase because of his aerial dominance at corners and free kicks. Bournemouth defenders Hill and Silva are low-owned alternatives, supported by strong defensive numbers and bonus-point potential.

Chelsea’s Cole Palmer remains a premium hold and buy for Leeds at home, followed by Forest and Palace, despite frustration over inconsistent returns. A Palmer-to-Bruno Fernandes move in Gameweek 14 is worth monitoring: Chelsea then face Liverpool and Manchester City, while Manchester United have Coventry and Palace, and Pochettino’s arrival could significantly raise Bruno’s appeal. Bruno is expensive and difficult to accommodate alongside Haaland and Palmer, so waiting through United’s Liverpool fixture is sensible. Kudus is also a high-upside differential but remains a watchlist option until Tottenham’s attack is more convincing.

Aston Villa’s upturn makes Suzuki an appealing goalkeeper for Sunderland at home and a favourable five-game run, though the cheaper Bugan offers outstanding value at £1.5m less and sits only three points behind Raya for the season. Matty Cash is an injury doubt, while Villa defensive options need checking for team news around Konsa and Saliba. Forest’s Milenkovic is a strong longer-term defensive target from Gameweek 13, when fixtures improve sharply. For midfield bargains, Rudoni is preferred below £5.5m, although McGinn offers a differential route and retains penalty duties.

The projected best Gameweek 11 XI is a 3-5-2: Suzuki; De Cuyper, Van Hecke, Vuskovic; Gross, Kudus, Palmer, Rogers, Sosa; Haaland and Jackson. A Gameweek 14 Free Hit is also a viable strategy for managers who want to retain Chelsea assets through one difficult fixture, then attack Manchester United’s home match with Coventry through a short-term triple-up.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham in Gameweek 11, with Jackson the leading alternative after returns in five of his last six matches.
Buy or hold Jackson for Chelsea’s five-match run from Sunderland at home through Coventry away, with a later switch to Joao Pedro worth considering when Chelsea’s fixtures worsen.
Gross is a premium Gameweek 11 midfield target at Hull thanks to penalties, set pieces and 10 goal involvements in 10 matches.
Hold De Cuyper for Brighton’s immediate fixtures, but favour Vuskovic as the safer new Brighton defensive purchase because Mitoma’s return could eventually affect De Cuyper’s minutes.
Suzuki is the leading goalkeeper pick, but Bugan is the value option at £1.5m cheaper and has a favourable Villa fixture run.
Palmer is worth keeping for Leeds, Forest and Palace, while a Gameweek 14 Palmer-to-Bruno Fernandes move becomes attractive if Pochettino improves Manchester United.
Barry is the preferred budget third striker over Evanilson due to his lower price and elite underlying numbers, although both are viable.
Consider saving a Free Hit for Gameweek 14 to target Manchester United’s home fixture against Coventry while temporarily avoiding Chelsea’s Liverpool match.

items.title: Tom's FPL GW11 Bus Team! 🚌
items.headline: Rolling remains the preferred move despite Manzambi temptation and a Barry-Silva bench call
items.summary:
With two free transfers and £1.6m in the bank, the current squad is in a position to roll rather than force a move. The overriding view is that, when there is no clear problem to solve, preserving flexibility is the sensible FPL play even if it feels unexciting.

Manzambi is the main potential transfer temptation, but there is no commitment to make the move with more than a week still available for further information. Holding the transfers keeps options open for injuries, price changes and fixture-driven moves closer to the deadline.

The immediate decision is likely to centre on the bench. Morgan Gibbs-White is set to start, leaving Barry and Silva competing for the remaining place. Starting Barry ahead of Silva is viewed as the higher-upside call, while accepting the risk that a more conservative selection could prove safer.
key_points: The squad has two free transfers and £1.6m available, so there is no immediate need to make a transfer.
Rolling at least one transfer is the preferred strategy unless a clearer reason to act emerges.
Manzambi is under consideration, but the move is not yet strong enough to justify sacrificing flexibility.
Morgan Gibbs-White is expected to start.
Starting Barry over Silva is the preferred upside benching decision.

items.title: ANOTHER GREEN ARROW ✅ | FPL CHAI'S GW11 TEAM REVEAL | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Gabriel-to-Luka move offers route to Jackson as Brighton defence dominates Gameweek 11 thinking
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 presents a rare opportunity to roll transfers for managers whose squads are already well positioned, despite the temptation to chase value defenders and new attacking options. The core team discussed features Kinsky; Gabriel, Silva and Kiper; Kudus, Rogers, Palmer, Gross and Manzambi; with Haaland captained alongside Barry. Calafiori is a viable substitute if Manzambi’s recurring calf issue restricts him, although Manzambi is still preferred if fit because attacking players with favourable home fixtures retain greater upside than defenders.

The main transfer dilemma is how to fund Nicolas Jackson. Gabriel to Luka is the most attractive structural move: Luka’s attacking threat, secure minutes and Brighton’s strong fixture run make him a cheaper alternative, while the sale would release funds to replace Gonzalo, whose prospects diminish with Muniz fit again. The drawback is giving up Gabriel’s Arsenal clean-sheet and set-piece potential, particularly if Saliba does not immediately displace Ezri Konsa. A more cautious route is to downgrade Manzambi only if his injury proves significant, but that means sacrificing an active attacking option for a cheap bench player.

Brighton’s defence is the biggest ownership concern. Verbruggen, Luka and Van Hecke offer excellent value, while Vuskovic is also viewed as a premium DefCon option. Van Hecke’s Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham and Hull fixtures, plus his attacking numbers and bonus potential, make him especially difficult to ignore. Muarevich is another reliable DefCon pick even in tougher fixtures, with Leeds proving defensively competitive against Arsenal, Manchester United and Spurs. The preferred defensive order is Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Muarevich and Silva, with the broader conclusion that inexpensive DefCon defenders can outscore more expensive names such as Gabriel or Calafiori over this stretch.

Jackson is the standout forward target, while Isak becomes increasingly appealing after scoring before the break and continuing to receive strong minutes for Liverpool. Manchester United’s appointment of Mauricio Pochettino also puts Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo back on the watchlist, although Liverpool in Gameweek 11 is a difficult immediate test. If United show signs of a bounce, Fernandes or Mbeumo become plausible Haaland alternatives for Gameweek 12, when Haaland faces Arsenal. Palmer remains a hold through Leeds, Forest and Crystal Palace despite Chelsea’s uneven form, as his explosive potential and fixtures outweigh the appeal of a premature move to Gross.

Free Hit planning shapes the next transfers. Gameweek 14 is the preferred window because Manchester United host Coventry, Leeds host Ipswich, Bournemouth host Hull and several current assets face awkward clashes, including Spurs v Arsenal and Chelsea v Liverpool. It offers a route into Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Bournemouth attackers and Leeds or Everton defensive options without committing to them long term. Gameweek 12 and 13 are alternatives, with Liverpool’s home match against Sunderland in Gameweek 13 particularly attractive for a triple-up, but Gameweek 14 best suits squads carrying Arsenal, Chelsea, Brighton and Spurs players.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 11, with Barry retained as a useful differential rather than forcing a transfer.
Consider Gabriel to Luka to unlock funds for Gonzalo to Nicolas Jackson; Brighton’s fixtures, clean-sheet form and Luka’s attacking numbers support the move.
Hold Cole Palmer through Leeds, Forest and Crystal Palace unless selling him directly enables a clearly superior restructuring move.
Monitor Manzambi’s calf injury: start Calafiori instead if Manzambi is unavailable or likely to play limited minutes.
Van Hecke, Vuskovic and Muarevich are leading DefCon defenders, with Van Hecke particularly attractive ahead of Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham and Hull.
Watch Manchester United under Pochettino before buying Bruno Fernandes or Bryan Mbeumo; Gameweek 12 can offer a route away from Haaland against Arsenal.
Isak is a strong forward alternative if Liverpool continue to give him 75-plus minutes, starting with Manchester United in Gameweek 11.
Target Free Hit Gameweek 14, when Manchester United play Coventry, Leeds play Ipswich and Bournemouth play Hull while several popular assets have difficult fixtures.
